objectives.title: Hear Eurylochus Out
objectives.hint: He stands at the class-post by the driftwood fire, a few steps up the sand from where you woke.

objectives.title: Drive Off the Drowned
objectives.hint: Three drowned haul themselves out of the surf at the waterline, west of the fire. Cut them down before they reach the crew.

objectives.title: Tell Eurylochus You Will Climb
objectives.hint: He is still at the fire, watching the smoke on the mountain. Give him the word to lead on.

npc/antiphos.doing: Sitting the fire out with his knees drawn up, sizing the mountain and saying nothing about it.
Sitting the fire out with his knees drawn up, sizing the mountain and saying nothing about it.

npc/elpenor.doing: Feeding the driftwood fire too fast and talking to keep the dark off his back.

npc/eurylochus.doing: Working the crew count in his head at the class-post and arguing the smoke to the captain's face before the order comes.
Working the crew count in his head at the class-post and arguing the smoke to the captain's face before the order comes.

obj/muster.text: The sun drops fast behind the world's rim, the way it does at sea. In the last red light, the surf begins to move.
The surf gives up its dead: three drowned wade out of the shallows toward the fire, and the last of the light goes out of the water behind them.

obj/surf.text: The last of them slides back under the foam. The beach is yours for as long as the light lasts.

obj/climb-out.text: Eurylochus shoulders a coil of rope and starts up the worn path. Follow the smoke.

on_complete.text: Antiphos hoists the wine and the meal-sacks onto one shoulder. "Somebody carries the man's dinner," he says, and falls in behind you. Elpenor stays with the fire — alone, and burning it high.

on_arrive.text: Antiphos sets the sacks down in the light of the mouth and stays there, catching his wind and counting lambs.

objectives.title: Follow Eurylochus to the Cave
objectives.hint: Climb up off the sand behind him: through the grazing meadow, past the low stone sheep-fold standing walled and empty, and up the switchbacks of the mountain's face to the smoking cave mouth where the great boulder rests.

npc/antiphos.doing: Setting the provision-sacks down in the light of the mouth, catching his wind and counting the pens off on one finger.
Setting the provision-sacks down in the light of the mouth, catching his wind and counting the pens off on one finger.

npc/elpenor.doing: Left holding the beach alone and burning the fire high enough to be seen from the ledge.

barks: Still burning, Captain! Told you I could keep a fire!
Every time that mountain makes a noise I put another log on. There is a lot of log gone.
If you are not down by first light I am coming up there. — I am not. But I have said it.

npc/eurylochus.doing: Leading the climb with a coil of rope on his shoulder, waiting on the ledge for the party to make the last switchback.
Leading the climb with a coil of rope on his shoulder, waiting on the ledge for the party to make the last switchback.

obj/reach-mouth.text: The mouth breathes cool air and old smoke. Eurylochus steps inside ahead of you.

objectives.title: Step Into the Cave
objectives.hint: Move in past the mouth to the first broad shelf of the hall, where the racks begin.

objectives.title: Take a Wheel of Cheese
objectives.hint: The cheese is racked on the shelves by the entry. Take a wheel from the barrel among them.

objectives.title: Decide With Eurylochus
objectives.hint: He is at your shoulder by the cheese racks. Tell him whether you run for the ship or wait for the owner of this cave.

npc/antiphos.doing: Holding the daylight at the mouth with the sacks, out of the dark on purpose.
Back at the strand with the sacks aboard and every man he climbed with still on his feet.

barks: Sacks are aboard, Captain. Everything we came in with, and one wheel to the good.
Say the word and I will shove her off. I would like very much to be rowing.
Still burning, Captain! Told you I could keep a fire!
Every time that mountain makes a noise I put another log on. There is a lot of log gone.

npc/elpenor.doing: Alone at the fire on the strand, keeping the one promise anybody gave him.
Standing over the fire he kept, with a speech prepared for a loss that never happened.

npc/eurylochus.doing: At the captain's shoulder among the racks, pricing the cheese and pressing for the decision to run.
At the gangplank counting the party aboard twice over, on the one branch of this island where the number comes out whole.

npc/perimedes.doing: Newly in at the party's heel with the ship's wine-skin, backed into the recess beside the racks and reading the whole hall once.
Down on the sand ahead of everyone with the wine-skin still unopened, working out whether the giant counts his cheeses.

on_respawn.text: You come to against the cold shelf inside the mouth, cheese-smell and old smoke in your throat.

obj/checkpoint.text: Cheese racked to the roof, lambs penned and sorted by age, the milk pails still warm on the shelf. Whoever keeps this house walked out of it this morning meaning to walk back in tonight.
Perimedes slips in at your heel with the ship's wine-skin on his shoulder, reads the whole hall once, and puts his back to the recess beside the racks.

obj/cheese.text: A wheel of hard yellow cheese, heavy as a shield. Perimedes presses the wine-skin from the ship into your other hand: "Carried it up myself, Captain. In case a stranger needs making a guest."

on_arrive.text: Perimedes is through the mouth before you finish speaking and down the path ahead of all of you, counting heads onto the sand as they arrive.
Antiphos shoulders the sacks without a word and starts down. Arithmetic, Captain: everything you came in with, and one wheel of cheese to the good.
Eurylochus comes down last with the rope still on his shoulder, stands at the gangplank and counts the party aboard one at a time, out loud, twice.
Eurylochus presses himself into the recess beside you, sword drawn and pointless, breathing through his teeth.

objectives.title: Run for the Ship
objectives.hint: Back down the mountain the way you climbed, past the fold and the fire, to the gangplank where the galley waits.

objectives.title: Board the Galley
objectives.hint: Cross the gangplank and take your place at the oars while the cave is still empty behind you.

obj/flee-back.text: Cheese in the crook of your arm, and behind you the lambs left complaining in their pens. Nobody will ever make a song of this one, Captain. You will simply get home.

obj/board-flee.text: Ithaca inside the month. Safe, and fed, and a little smaller for it — and every man you came in with still at his oar.

objectives.title: Get Into the Shadows
objectives.hint: The light is going and something is coming up the slope. Press into one of the dark recesses along the hall wall, and watch.

objectives.title: Find Perimedes in the Dark
objectives.hint: When the stone is down and the giant sits to his milking, find Perimedes pressed into the recess beside the racks and learn what walked in.

npc/antiphos.doing: Standing in the light of the mouth with the sacks when the herdsman comes home, and the first thing the giant reaches for.
Back at the strand with the sacks aboard and every man he climbed with still on his feet.

npc/perimedes.doing: Flat in the recess by the racks, watching the mouth and putting the whole scene to memory because he cannot stop himself.
Down on the sand ahead of everyone with the wine-skin still unopened, working out whether the giant counts his cheeses.

obj/take-cover.text: Stay in the shadows and watch. What comes home now was never yours to fight.

effects.text: He picks a man up by the ankle without looking, the way a man rights a kicked-over pail. It is Antiphos. No one has time to make a sound.
Stone grinds across the mouth. The daylight narrows to a line, then to nothing.

on_respawn.text: You come to in the dark by the racks. The giant is a shape at his own fire, milking, unhurried.

obj/the-stone.text: "One eye, middle of the forehead, and he talks like a man — asked us who we were, polite as you like. The stone took twenty-two waggons to set and he rolled it one-handed. We do not fight him, Captain. We think."

objectives.title: Meet the Owner of the Cave
objectives.hint: Polyphemus sits at the great fire at the heart of the hall. Go to him before you touch anything else of his, and mind your manners about the wine.

npc/polyphemus.doing: Milking at his own fire, entertaining the talking meat, and asking a guest for the one thing a guest cannot refuse.
Gone over at his own fire with the cup spilled, saying the flock and the wine and the promise out loud in his sleep.

barks: ...mm. The grey ewe. Grey ewe first, then the black one, then...
...more. Give me it again. Again...
...last. I said last. I keep my word, little...
...no. No, father. They were only men. They were only men, they were...

obj/the-name.text: The wine of Maron does its work. His chin sinks to his chest, and the whole cave fills with the long tide of his breathing.

on_complete.text: Perimedes drags a beam of green olive-wood from the giant's stacked timber and puts it in your hands. "Big as a mast, Captain. We cut it down to a point."

objectives.missing_item_hint: The wheel turns under your palm, takes a slow full circle and bites on nothing at all.
objectives.title: Grind the Point
objectives.hint: The giant keeps a grinding stone under the light-shaft on the west floor. Turn the olive beam against it until it takes an edge.

objectives.title: Char It in the Fire
objectives.hint: Take the sharpened stake to the great walled hearth at the heart of the hall and turn the point in the coals until it blackens hard.

objectives.missing_item_hint: You lay a hand on the great closed lid. It is warm, and it moves. The giant talks up out of the wine without waking: "...mm. Not yet. The black one is still to milk..." — and your hand, which is only a hand, comes away.
objectives.title: Put Out the Eye
objectives.hint: He is down where the wine took him, at his own fire. Set the hardened point to the single eye and lean your whole weight on it.

objectives.title: Climb Toward the Pen
objectives.hint: Leave him roaring at the floor and slip from shadow to shadow up the rock ramp toward the upper sheep-pen. Do not run and do not jump; he hunts by sound now.

npc/polyphemus.doing: Asleep at his fire with the wine in him, talking through it, while the point is ground and charred in his own hearth.

obj/blind.text: The hills answer him. His own kind call in at the stone: "Polyphemus! Who is killing you?" And he roars his ruined face against the rock: "NOBODY! Nobody is killing me!" A pause. Then, going away up the mountain: "If nobody hurts you, it is a sickness from Zeus. Pray to your father." And the footsteps do not come back. He hears them go.

The hills answer him. His own kind call in: "Polyphemus! Who has done this?" And he roars back the name you laid down over the wine, whole and proud: "ODYSSEUS! Sacker of cities, son of Laertes, of Ithaca — he was under my roof!" And they believe him. "Hold, cousin — we cannot shift your stone from without. Wait for the light; at dawn every hand on the mountain opens it together." Perimedes has your sleeve: "They come back at dawn, Captain. We leave before they do."

The hills answer him. His own kind call in: "Polyphemus! Who has done this?" And he roars back the name you gave him over the wine: "AITHON! A Cretan, out of Crete — at my own fire!" A silence. Then, cool and turning away: "A Cretan. Cousin, the Cretans lie; it is the one thing known of them. Sleep it off." And the footsteps go, half-convinced of nothing, and do not come back tonight.

on_respawn.text: You come to below the ramp. The blind giant is still pacing the cavern floor, hands out, listening.

effects.text: Get up the ramp. Make no sound he can follow.

on_caught.text: His head snaps toward you. Freeze — get back into a shadow.

obj/climb-to-pen.text: The rams crowd the upper pen, warm and stupid and enormous. Below you the giant paces the floor he can no longer see.

objectives.title: Get Under a Ram
objectives.hint: Take two fistfuls of fleece at the belly of the biggest ram and let it carry you, close and quiet, when the flock goes out.

npc/perimedes.doing: Third ram from the gate, talking the captain in under the belly of the biggest one.

effects.text: Stone grinds back off the mouth, and the first daylight in a day and a night comes down the hall in one white bar.
He settles himself against the rock beside the gap and puts his hands out over it, running them along every back that passes. Only the backs. He never thinks to feel underneath.
Daylight, and salt air. The ram carries you out under the giant's very hands and down the mountain toward the sea.

objectives.title: Down to the Ship
objectives.hint: Come down off the mountain to the strand where the galley rides at her gangplank, oars manned and waiting.

objectives.title: Board and Give Way
objectives.hint: Cross the gangplank to the deck and take your place. However you leave him, the water is listening.

npc/elpenor.doing: Standing over a fire he kept all night, counting the party back down the path and asking the one question nobody wants to answer.
Standing over the fire he kept, with a speech prepared for a loss that never happened.

npc/eurylochus.doing: At the gangplank counting heads out loud for the third time and refusing to grieve until the oars are moving.

npc/perimedes.doing: On the sand with two fists of ram's wool still in them, laughing wrong and asking to be told the count is four.

obj/last-sand.text: Behind you, high on the mountain, the blind giant has not gone back inside. He has set himself across the mouth of his own cave with his hands out and his head turned, waiting for a sound to hate. Whatever is still in there is his now.

obj/board-nobody.text: Oars out, and the strand slides away astern. Nobody looks back at the mountain; there is a great deal of open water to be got between you and it before anyone feels like talking.

objectives.title: Take Your Place at the Oar
objectives.hint: The island is astern and going. Find your bench and let the water do the rest.

obj/aboard.text: Open water on every side, and the oars finding their stroke. Somewhere behind the dark the island is still there, and it is already somebody else's problem.

effects.text: You won the cave. He will tell the story to the end of his days and never once get the name right, and the neighbours who came as far as the stone have gone back to their own fires believing a sickness took him. No song, no herald, no one ashore who will ever hear it. You will live on that. You will have to.

You won the cave, and then you signed it. Somewhere astern the mountain is awake — hands on the slope, cousin calling to cousin, every one of them coming at first light to lift the stone off a man who can now give the sea your name and your father's. Eurylochus has the stroke going and will not look back. Whatever you bought in there, the water will come to collect.

You won the cave, and a Cretan took the credit. The hills heard the name, weighed it and went back to sleep — a trader out of Crete, and Cretans lie, so nothing worth waking for was said at all. No one is coming for Aithon; there was never an Aithon to come for. You have your crew, your water and a clean horizon, and the best hour of your life belongs to a man who does not exist.
You set your shoulder to the great stone. It does not so much as grind. No blade you carry will bite it — whatever opens this cave, it will not be you.
Never strike a sleeping god's son. He comes up off the floor with his whole strength, and there is nothing in this cave that can stand against that.
Your blade turns on his hide like a stick on a ship's keel. He sets down the pail. Slowly. In his own house, under his own stone, you have raised a hand to him — and he rises to answer it in full.
Your foot turns a pebble in the mouth of the cave and his head comes round on the sound like a door slamming. He told the hills he would eat you last. He did not say he had stopped.
